findings.evidence: roadmap SpinRepresentations/Suggested.lean `SpinPolarizationData` fields `isotropic_W`, `pairing_nondegenerate_left/right`, `line_orthogonal` all use `QuadraticMap.polar Q`; Hyperbolic.lean:85 `private theorem hyperbolicModelForm_associated_apply`.
findings.fix: Add a public `hyperbolicModelForm_polar_apply : polar (hyperbolicModelForm R n) x y = x.1.1 y.1.2 + y.1.1 x.1.2 + 2 * ∑ i, x.2 i * y.2 i` (needs only `CommRing`, no `Invertible (2 : K)`), mark it `@[simp]`, and derive the existing `associated` version from it — or simply make `hyperbolicModelForm_associated_apply` public.
findings.issue: `hyperbolicModelForm_associated_apply` is `private`, so the public surface has no bilinear/polar characterization of `hyperbolicModelForm`. The stated consumer `SpinPolarizationData` states isotropy and pairing nondegeneracy entirely via `QuadraticMap.polar Q x y`, and the sibling file exposes exactly this shape publicly (`Standard.lean:48 polarBilin_weightedSumSquares`, `:62 polarBilin_weightedSumSquares_one` with `@[simp]`).

findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/AlgClosed.lean:52 `theorem equivalent_weightedSumSquares_of_isAlgClosed ... Equivalent Q (weightedSumSquares K (1 : Fin (Module.finrank K M) → K))` is public; Hyperbolic.lean:76 states the same conclusion under `[IsSepClosed K]`.
findings.fix: Make it public (e.g. `equivalent_weightedSumSquares_of_isSepClosed`, mirroring the Mathlib name); `isometryEquivSumSquaresUnits` may stay private once it is exposed.
findings.issue: `equivalentSumSquares` (nondegenerate finite-dimensional form over a separably closed field with `2` invertible is equivalent to the sum of squares) is `private`. It is a strict generalization of Mathlib's public `QuadraticForm.equivalent_weightedSumSquares_of_isAlgClosed` and is the reusable general result this PR actually contributes; hiding it forces the next consumer to re-prove it.

summary: The model form's bilinear/polar characterization is private, so the roadmap consumer (whose isotropy and pairing conditions are all stated in QuadraticMap.polar) has no public lemma for it; the sep-closed sum-of-squares normalization, a strict generalization of a public Mathlib theorem, is also hidden.
